chapters.summary: Architect Marco Tomayo proposes mandating geothermal systems for new buildings to eliminate conventional cooling towers, arguing this reduces Legionella risk at the source while also cutting energy consumption and complying with Local Law 97.
chapters.title: Marco Tomayo proposes geothermal systems to eliminate cooling towers

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Chair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: My name is Marco Tomayo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: I'm an architect, resident of the Opry side.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: I'm an expert in sustainability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: The recent Legionella outbreak in our community should make us reconsider how we design and operate our buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: Cooling towers require continuous maintenance, water treatment, inspections, and strict regulatory compliance like you are doing today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: But even the strictest regulations cannot completely eliminate the human error.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: Rather than relying on better maintenance, we should consider a technology that reduces the source of risk.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: Geothermal systems can provide heating and cooling without conventional cooling towers, reducing the potential for legionella exposure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: Geothermal systems also require less mechanical room spaces, reducing equipment and infrastructure at the top of the buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: At the same time, geothermal systems substantially reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions, helping buildings comply with the New York City Local Law 97, which requires reductions in building emissions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: Although initial construction costs may increase by approximately 17%, long-term energy and maintenance savings can make this investment economically worthwhile.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: For these reasons, I propose that geothermal systems shall be mandatory for new buildings and projects receiving discretionary approval in these chambers, where they can replace

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: conventional cooling towers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: This is not about replacing regulations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: It is about eliminating.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: unnecessary risk at their source while creating buildings that are healthier, safer, lower carbon, and more efficient.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Marco Tomayo
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Next.

chapters.summary: Water treatment professional William Spitz discusses issues with towers idle during construction, recommends draining towers until put into service, supports three annual cleanings, and suggests changing 31-day testing to monthly not exceeding 40 days with a grace period.
chapters.title: William Spitz on water treatment practices and tower idle periods

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I am William Spitz.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I have a degree in mechanical engineering from NYU.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I've been in the water treatment business since 1971.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: In 1983, I started Wesco Technologies.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And in 2025, I merged with Metro Group, a larger company servicing some 1,000 New York City cooling towers.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I applaud New York City's proactive response to the 2015 Legionnaires outbreak.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Previous to the enactment of Law 77, one out of 10 of our clients would allow us to disinfect and clean their towers once a year.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The local law

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: is good but not perfect.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: It is my understanding that the Harlem outbreak in 2025 involved Harlem Hospital and an adjacent construction site.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The Harlem outbreak brings up two issues.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Harlem Hospital is owned by New York City.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Do New York City-owned properties adhere to Local Law 77?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And are they inspected?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The second, how do you treat a tower in new construction sites?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Typically, the towers are installed, and when the piping and refrigeration equipment are in place, they are flushed with an alkaline cleaner and disinfected and cleaned.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Then they may be idle for up to a year.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Before they are put into service.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: It's hard to treat a tower that's not operating.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I would recommend having towers drained until they are put into service, and when they are going to be operated, they should be disinfected and cleaned per Local Law 77 and registered with the DOH.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I concur with the proposal that the towels should be cleaned three times each year.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: You need to summarize the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The disinfection and cleaning should be done in spring, summer, and fall.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The summer disinfection should replace the summertime hyperhalogenation.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Legionella testing every 31 days should be changed to monthly, not to exceed 40 days.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Water treatment companies are in partnership with the city.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: It's hard to keep track of 31-day intervals.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: for each of the thousands of towers.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: With respect to the fines, I recommend a five-day grace period.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Meter regulations allow a five-minute grace period and speed cameras up to 10 miles leeway.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The city used Q...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: You need to...

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: You need to wrap it up.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The city used PCR tests to preliminary test the towers.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: These tests do not distinguish between living and dead organisms.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: It's a useful tool.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The actual tests can be performed in the field in as low as 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: That level of detail, I can't, we have to go on to the other people.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So please submit your testimony to us.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: And I heard earlier today the health department speak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: And it was quite frustrating to hear the things that they were saying that were not actually happening in reality for those of us that were experiencing Legionnaires.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I want to note that when we first found out that we had Legionnaires in our building, when the health department showed up, they sent one community health worker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: She did not understand what she was talking about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: She shared incorrect information with us, which I think leads to the...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I saw in the legislation regarding having a hotline, right, where people can speak to those who understand what Legionnaires is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: The fact that you had a community health worker show up, and she was speaking so cavalier about this, about the fact that we had Legionnaires in our building, and was not providing any resources.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: She had no literature with her.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: She had nothing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: She just had herself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: And as she was speaking, the management was there, and we asked them, I said, what are you going to provide in regards to a timeline regarding how you're going to address this issue?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: Because now you're telling us that we're going to have water restrictions in our building, and this is during the wintertime, telling us that we can't use our hot water, telling us that we have to take cold showers and a cold bath.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: That part.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I don't know if you've ever had to use a shower hose, which is literally the same hose that you use when you're out in your back garden to shower yourself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: It is the most demeaning thing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: And as someone that has literally migrated here from another country, I come here to not have to deal with those things.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: And it's extremely frustrating to have to literally shower with a shower hose.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: So thank you for mentioning that because that was disgusting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: Let me just say these last things, a couple of things that I do really want to mention about the failures of the health department, because I think that when they were up here, they were just being disingenuous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: When they showed up to our meeting, they did not have, our building has predominantly Spanish speakers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: They had nobody there to translate in Spanish the health issues around what Legionnaires were.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: They had to have a resident from our building translate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: health issues, like talking about Legionnaires, and there was massive confusion in that meeting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: In addition to that, the fact that nobody from Mayor Mamdani's office showed up was disturbing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: To this date, nobody from his office has showed up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: And the fact that we have the conversations around what are the resources that you're going to provide residents post-putting water restrictions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I don't care that you're giving free U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: Open tickets for $100.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: For the last six months, I've had to accumulate an additional cost.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I've had to go to the hairdresser to shower, to wash my hair.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I've had to go to friends'houses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I've had to buy water.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I've had to get a gym membership that has a shower.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: All of these additional costs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I'm currently in housing court because our landlord refuses to give us a discount on our rent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: These are the things that are just extremely frustrating.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: In addition to that, the health department has not shown up since that time that we had the meeting because we had a huge press conference.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: And I really want to shout out the Harlem Legionnaires Task Force because if it wasn't for them and their support, we would have been drowning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: We would have had no attention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: We would have had nothing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: But it was us as residents that stood together to stand up and the failures of the fact that Mayor Mamdani and the health department, they have not shown up once since that meeting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: They have not tabled.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: And to hear that the Upper East Side has had all of these resources, but those of us in West Harlem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: Black and brown people have not had anything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: It's disgusting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: And honestly, I want to call out also our councilwoman, Shaun-Abreu.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I haven't heard from him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I haven't seen him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: He hasn't said anything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: We don't even know where we are.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I am still under current water restrictions.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I'll bring this back.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: But I just want to make sure that you guys bring this back to the health department.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: I just want to make sure that they have additional training for their staff because their staff does not understand what Legionnaires is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: They don't understand what equity is when it comes to addressing health concerns in black and brown communities, which means that you should have translators, that you should have materials that are speaking in Spanish and other languages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: The simple fact that these little things are not being done post what's being happened is disgusting to me.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: And the last time they showed up to our building, which was like a couple months ago,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Heven Barhanet
utterances.text: the person that was tabling didn't know why they were there.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you for sharing that.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: But make sure, please make sure to submit something.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: It's testimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And you can, if you forget, you can go up on the council website.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: It's there.

chapters.summary: Kim Smith, founder of the Harlem Legionnaires Task Force, expresses condolences to Upper East Side families, calls for greater accountability and enforcement, and questions whether 56 water ecologists are sufficient for 5,000 cooling towers. She hopes 2027 won't be a trifecta of outbreaks.
chapters.title: Kim Smith of Harlem Task Force calls for accountability and more inspectors

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: Hello, I am Kim Smith, founder of the Harlem Legionnaires Task Force.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: Once again, thank you, Chair Shulman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: I was here last year testifying with another founding member of the Harlem Legionnaires Task Force.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: So I'm here first and foremost to extend my deepest condolences.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: When I heard of the first deaths on the Upper East Side, I literally wept.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: Because it's a

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: It didn't make a difference because it occurred on the Upper East Side.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: It's humanity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: When it happened last year in 2025, we were literally petrified in our community because we didn't receive all of the information that, thankfully, the Upper East Side is receiving.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: And I've said to our community, because we had our senator advocating on our

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: behalf, and we worked closely with the former administration to make sure that we said, God forbid, if this were to happen again, please give information.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: And that has been done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: So I keep saying we have to make sure that we highlight the pros and the cons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: So I'm just hoping, A, that we get greater accountability, greater enforcement, more transparency, because I'm concerned it's about...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: 5,000 cooling towers across the five boroughs and 56 water ecologists are supposed to be enough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: Like right there, I'm saying to myself, wow, there may need to be more.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: That's very minimal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: And additionally, how to ensure that information is disseminated properly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: Like when they had their issue at 3333, you know, I reached out to contacts at the health department to say, hey.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: You know, they may not understand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: And thankfully, with the rapport that we've built, the Legionnaires Task Force, DOHMH, they did step up.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: They made sure of that stuff.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: But it can be more at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: So I just wanted to say I'm here because I pray to God that 2027 is not a trifecta.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: We had 25, 26.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Kim Smith
utterances.text: We hope nothing in 2027.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And we'll take all of this back.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So I really appreciate both of you giving that testimony.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And I do remember the address because I get notified as the chair of the committee about, so I remember when this happened.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: But I'm sorry that it's still happening.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: So I'll take a look too.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you both.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: We will now move to virtual testimony.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Please wait for your name to be called to testify and please select unmute when prompted.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Please keep the testimony to two minutes.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: If you have lengthy testimony, you could submit it to testimony at council.nyc.gov within 72 hours of the end of this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: The first person.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: We have is Ronald Katter, K-A-T-T-E-R.

chapters.summary: Attorney Ronald Katter represents Ida Goldstein and the family of Judge Charles Thomas, calling for strict enforcement and accountability from both cooling tower owners and DOHMH. He argues unenforced laws cannot remedy the recurring plague of Legionnaires' disease.
chapters.title: Ronald Katter represents victims' families, demands enforcement and accountability

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Speaker Manin, Chair Shulman, and members of the Committee on Health.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: My name is Ronald Catter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: I am here today to give a voice to Upper East Side residents who were poisoned

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: by Legionnaire's disease, an invisible recurring menace, and to hold negligent cooling tower owners and the Department of Health accountable for the lives they failed to protect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: I represent many Upper East Side residents who were sickened, who suffered, and who now live with the long-term consequences of this disease, as well as the families of loved ones who's...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: Loved ones were tragically and fatally succumbed to the illness.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: My clients'lives have been permanently shattered by this summer's preventable Legionnaire disease outbreak, leaving them with severe, lifelong trauma.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: Behind the Department of Health's clinical statistics, with its reported 94 cases and 11 deaths, are real New Yorkers whose futures were stolen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: I represent Ida Goldstein, the widow and sole survivor of her late husband, Robert, a proud Air Force veteran and retired security consultant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: Their vibrant 50-year marriage and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: and future plans were abruptly stolen, leaving Ida to suffer profound loss and injury all alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: I also represent the loved ones of retired Judge Charles Thomas.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: Judge Thomas spent his life serving the public and intended to fully enjoy his retirement

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: surrounded by his family, friends, and music.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: Instead, his song was cut short by a toxic mist.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: This tragedy stems from a profound shared responsibility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: First, the cooling tower owners failed fundamentally.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: They are legally required to properly inspect and maintain their cooling towers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: So they could not just summarize, sir.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: Instead, they allowed their machinery to broadcast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN
utterances.text: Can you summarize so we have to move on?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: The health department shares equal culpability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: They failed to ensure towers were registered, failed to conduct annual inspections, and were severely understaffed when the outbreak hit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: And this is my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: After the 2015 Bronx Opera House outbreak, the city enacted cooling tower regulations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: After last year's Central Harlem outbreak, it made them stricter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: How can laws that are not enforced remedy this dire problem?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: A Department of Health that cannot cure a recurring annual plague is failing to protect the very lives of its citizens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: We demand strict enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: and immediate accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ronald Katter
utterances.text: Thank you for giving me this opportunity.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And you can submit the length of testimony to us at testimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Next is Dimitri Daskalakis.

chapters.summary: Dr. Demetrius Daskalakis, a public health professional, describes best practices for Legionella response including fast action, clear communication, and decisive remediation. He urges oversight rooted in programmatic improvement and warns against treating public health workers as targets.
chapters.title: Dr. Demetrius Daskalakis on outbreak response best practices and trust

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: Good afternoon, and thank you, Chair Shulman.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: I'm Dr.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: Demetrius Daskalakis, a physician and public health professional who has helped lead responses to Legionella and other communicable disease emergencies in New York City and nationally.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: First, I want to express my deepest sympathy to the families who lost loved ones and to every New Yorker who became ill or afraid during this outbreak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: Every death matters, every hospitalization matters, and every family deserves answers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: Legionella outbreaks are hard.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: They move quickly, they require action before every answer is known, and they demand coordination among clinicians, epidemiologists, laboratorians, inspectors, building owners, communications teams, and community leaders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: Best practice is to move fast, communicate clearly, and act on evidence, identify possible environmental sources,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: test cooling towers and other water systems, issue clinician alerts, tell residents what symptoms to watch for, and make sure people with fever, cough, shortness of breath, muscle aches, or confusion seek care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: When a Legionella positive cooling tower in the outbreak geography is associated with cases and Legionella is detected, the response must be decisive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: Remediation means taking the tower offline when indicated and fully

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: cleaning and disinfecting it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: A shock treatment or temporary biocide boost may reduce risk in the moment, but it is not the same as a complete remediation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: The goal is not symbolic action.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: The goal is control of the outbreak and prevention of the next one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: I'm excited to be here today because oversight has a very important role.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: But I urge that oversight be rooted in the spirit of programmatic improvement and outbreak experience.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: Ask what worked, what did not, where regulations, inspections, reporting systems, communication, or resources can be strengthened, and how the city can respond even faster next time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: This is accountability, and it's also how public health gets better.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: During an outbreak, trust is not a luxury.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: It's a control measure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: Public health workers should be questioned, audited, and held accountable as they are being today by city council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: But they should not be treated as targets by clickbait-seeking media outlets that distort messaging from elected officials and health leaders while they're working to protect New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: Your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: No, just finish, Demetri.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: It's okay.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: Transparent communication and continuous improvement will save lives.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: That should be the shared objective as elected officials and public health experts and practitioners continue to improve how our city responds to this ubiquitous health threat.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Demetrius Daskalakis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Megan Peterson, president of DC 37 Local 3005, testifies that water ecologist salaries start at $52,000—too low for NYC living costs. She criticizes OMB for delaying hiring over a year, using slow hiring as a budget savings mechanism, and excluding staff from flexible work pilots.
chapters.title: Megan Peterson of DC 37 on water ecologist pay and OMB hiring delays

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Next is Megan Peterson.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: My name is Megan Peterson and I'm the president of DC 37, Local 3005.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: We represent scientists, including water ecologists at the health department.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: I am testifying about labor issues that are impacting recruitment and retention of inspectors, which are longstanding and predate the present administration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: The city could not recruit a full headcount of water ecologists because the salaries are too low to live on in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: As of July 15th, the city was advertising level one positions for a starting salary of $52,000 per year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: These staff are told that they should serve New York when they cannot afford housing costs in the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: While the union was recently awarded equity funds to modestly increase the salary, water ecologists have expressed to me that they are worried that new hires will leave.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: Staffing problems will persist so long as the salary is not competitive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: Secondly, OMB delays prevented timely staff recruitment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: OMB regularly takes over a year to approve candidates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: This was a best-case scenario with media attention from last summer's outbreak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: Still, the Monday after the outbreak was announced, a group of water ecologists were finally approved for onboarding by OMB.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: Dragging out hiring is often used by the city as a mechanism to save costs, and it must end.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: For instance, the fiscal 2027 executive budget plan includes savings of $2.5 million in FIS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: 2026 due to slower than anticipated ramp up of Legionella prevention funded in November 2025.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: The agency stated these savings would not result in any programmatic impact.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: However, we saw this was not the case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: Using drawn out hiring timelines as a budgeting trick is harming our neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: OMB delays are also a major reason for the privatization of city services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: As the agency will hire contracted services to circumvent hiring delays.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: Third, water ecologists level two and below have been left out of the flexible work pilot that was bargained in 2023 between the city and DC 37.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: Flexible scheduling and benefits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Can you summarize the rest of it and then submit it and submit whatever else you have?

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: Yeah, the summary is that these staff were left out of the flexible work pilot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: They could increase the number of inspections that they're doing in a week.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: If they had flexible scheduling from 10 inspections to 12 per week, which would really increase the amount.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: We need labor relations to seriously talk with us in the union in good faith about working conditions in the position.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: I'll forward the rest of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Megan Peterson
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Really appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: William McQuaid.

chapters.summary: Bill McQuaid, past president of ASHRAE, argues cooling towers get water from the potable water system and that 96% of cases are sporadic. He urges NYC to adopt a comprehensive source-to-tap strategy using ASHRAE standards rather than focusing exclusively on cooling towers.
chapters.title: Bill McQuaid of ASHRAE on source-to-tap prevention strategy

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: Chairman Shulman and members of the Committee on Health, thank you for the opportunity to testify today on New York City's response to the 2026 Legionella disease cluster.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: My name is Bill McQuaid.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: I've been a professional engineer in Pennsylvania for 28 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: I'm also a fellow, a distinguished lecturer, and the immediate past president of the American Society of Heating, Refrigeration, and Air Conditioning Engineers, also known as ASHRAE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: ASHRAE standards and guidelines are used around the world to help building owners, engineers, public health officials, and operators reduce risk in the built environment, including the risk of Legionnaire's disease.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: The central lesson from New York City's experience is that prevention cannot be limited to one device or one point in the system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: Cooling towers matter, and compliance with existing requirements is important, but a cooling tower approach has clearly not been enough.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: Most Legionnaires disease cases are not part of large outbreaks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: In fact, the CDC has found that 96% of all cases are sporadic and not associated with an outbreak.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: The thing that connects all of them is the potable water system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: Exposure can occur through many water-using components in that system, including building plumbing, showers, faucets, decorative fountain water features, hot water,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: hot tubs, humidifiers, and many other aerosol generating equipment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: I heard the health department officials say that cooling towers are separate from the potable water system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: This is absolutely not correct.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: Cooling towers get their water from the potable water system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: That is how it gets into the cooling towers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: It's a waterborne disease.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: It does not come from the air.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: That is why ASHRAE urges New York City to move toward a comprehensive source-to-tap strategy, just as we did 10 years ago when the outbreak occurred in the South Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: A fundamental approach in disease prevention is the precautionary principle.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: Yeah, Tom, as a can you summarize, please?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: This means that risk must be managed from the water source to the public distribution system into the building plumbing and finally to the fixtures and equipment where people may be exposed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: Municipal water quality, disinfection residuals, pressure changes, construction main breaks, treatment changes, storms, and building conditions can all have an influence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: Can all influence risk and must be managed.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: And you can submit more extended testimony at testimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: Yeah, I've already done that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Bill McQuaid
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: John Mullen.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: You may begin.

utterances.speaker: Lynn C. Schulman
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: John Mullen of IAPMO urges full adoption of ASHRAE Standard 188 and Guideline 12, plus ASSE Series 12000 training standards for plumbing and maintenance personnel. He argues building water management plans and certified staff can prevent outbreaks and reduce burden on health inspectors.
chapters.title: John Mullen of IAPMO on building water management standards

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: How are you doing?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: My name is John Mullen, and I'm here today to speak in favor of enhanced remediation efforts to combat the growth of Legionella, the bacteria that caused Legionnaire's disease.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: I serve as director of technical services for the International Association of Plumbing and Mechanical Officials, also known as IATMO.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: IATMO supports the implementation of stronger laws and regulations to combat the growth and spread of bacteria.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: The recent outbreak in New York City's Upper East Side with over 90 cases and at least 11 deaths following last year's deadly outbreak in Harlem clearly demonstrates the effort undertaken by

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: and a city to mitigate the bacteria has not been sufficient.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: This is likely attributable to in part the fact that the building water systems can serve as environmental opportunistic pathogens to proliferate, and aspects have not been fully sufficient addressed in other current mitigations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: As the City Council considers additional steps to alleviate the building outbreaks, IAPMO encourages the city to use best practices available to lead Janela remediation and building water systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: This includes the full adoption of the ASHRAE Standard 188 and ASHRAE Standard Guideline 12.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: Additionally, the ASSE Series 12000, particularly the Standard 12061 and Standard 12080,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: these establish unique training programs to educate the pipe trades, craftspeople, employers, building water management teams, and other construction maintenance personnel on how to effectively, safely in their environments with potential exposure to these pathogens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: These evidence-based practices have been designated by the National Standard Institute for Canada and also the SCC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: We strongly encourage passing stronger legislation with fully adopting these standards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: The importance of having building water management plans cannot be overstated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: Having staff certified with these ASC standards can regularly test water outlets, and it can help prevent future outbreaks and take some of the burden off the health inspectors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: So I am here to provide any additional information to the staff and committee you might have on this situation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - John Mullen
utterances.text: Thank you for your time and consideration today.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: And if you have more testimony, you can actually submit it at testimony at council.nyc.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You have 72 hours.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You can do that.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: So if you want to give us more information, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

summary: Oversight hearing on the 2026 Upper East Side Legionnaires' disease cluster that sickened 94 and killed 11 New Yorkers, examining DOHMH's response and preparedness
Committee considers eight bills to strengthen cooling tower inspections, public education, testing access, and enforcement of Legionella prevention laws
Family members of victims, community advocates, and industry experts testify on enforcement failures, communication gaps, and needed reforms including source-to-tap water system testing
